packages.fixSummary: Theme replay skip + rAF-coalesced refresh: ThemePresenter.apply() now computes a content-only signature (colorScheme plus order-independent token pairs) and returns early when it equals the last applied signature AND landingIntact() proves the document still holds exactly that state, so provably-idempotent snapshot replays no longer re-write every CSS variable. In addition the expensive getComputedStyle(body).backgroundColor read (which forces a synchronous document-wide style recalculation) is moved out of the synchronous publish dispatch into a requestAnimationFrame callback, merged across a whole dispatch round and all presenters into a single read, with an inline fallback when the host cannot schedule frames.

packages.fixSummary: Wallpaper content comparison for the shading override layer: the overrideTokens payload is now built into a local 'next' object and compared field-by-field against the tokens last handed to ui-theme (shadedTokens / sameShadedTokens). When the shade content is unchanged - which it is on every theme change because the layer is rebuilt byte-identically - the function returns early, keeping the existing override layer and skipping the dispose + re-register cycle that re-enters every theme/change listener (the source of the redundant publish storm).

packages.fixSummary: Subagent-projection carry-forward narrowing + key-set gate (P2-AC). The previous projection's extra byId rows are now carried forward only for ids that a visited address-chain step genuinely needs (chainRowIds), instead of every extra key; and whole-object reuse of the previous byId is only taken when the previous key set has exactly the same length as the live key set and every live key is present. This prevents stale subagent rows from being resurrected and prevents an unsound byId object identity reuse that left the UI projection inconsistent.

packages.fixSummary: Usage/R4 lifecycle hardening against stale async responses. A monotonic per-loader generation counter plus an aliveRef unmount flag are added; every RPC completion is now gated by current() = aliveRef.current && generation === <thatLoader>GenerationRef.current, so responses from a superseded request round, and any response arriving after unmount/remount, are discarded instead of calling setState. The effect re-arms aliveRef on setup (StrictMode setup->cleanup->setup safe) and cleanup bumps all three generations so an in-flight request from the previous mount can never resurrect state.

discrepancies.title: ?rev= is a browser cache-buster only; the server ignores it for content selection
discrepancies.detail: Requesting /plugins/@local/dsh-wallpaper/client.js?rev=deadbeef0000 returned HTTP 200 with the identical 31803 bytes. All four bundles are served with 'cache-control: no-cache' (no ETag, no immutable/max-age).
discrepancies.practicalImpact: Stale-serving is not prevented by the rev string server-side; it is prevented by no-cache forcing revalidation. Since served bytes == on-disk bytes == the fixed file, there is no stale-content risk at the HTTP layer right now. A browser could still hold a previously-executed module in memory until reload, which is what the in-page markers below are designed to detect.
